contexts.text: The ploughman reaching the reaper (). Explained.
In which shall be neither ploughing nor harvest () = no appearance of good and the derivative truth. Ploughing = preparation from good to receive truths.

The reason ploughing = good, is that a field, which is ploughed, = the Church as to good... Hence to plough = preparation from good to receive truths. The oxen, too, with which [the ground] was ploughed = goods in the Natural.

As this was the signification of ploughing, it was forbidden to plough with an ox and a donkey together ()... To plough with an ox = good in the Natural; and to plough with a donkey = truth there... (and) the Angels could not have a separate idea of good and truth... and therefore did not want to look at such ploughing.
That to plough, etc. = such things as are of good and its truth. Illustrated.

No one putting his hand to the plough, but looking backwards, is disposed for the Kingdom of God () = ... let not him who is in good, betake himself thence to those things which are of the doctrinals of faith.
It was on this account that it displeased Elijah, that Elisha, who was in the field ploughing, when called, asked that he might first kiss his father and mother...
In the opposite sense, ploughing = the evil which destroys good; thus vastation; as in .
In ploughing and in reaping thou shalt rest () = as to the implantation of truth in good, and its reception. Ploughing = the implantation of truth in good.

The reason ploughing = the implantation of truth in good, is that by a field is signified the Church as to good; thus the good of the Church; and by the seed which is inseminated, is signified the truth of faith.
Will the plougher plough the whole day to sow... ()... describes the reformation and regeneration of the man of the Church... To plough = to implant truth in good.
That ploughing, from correspondence, = the first of the Church in general; and also in particular with everyone who is being regenerated. Illustrated.

To plough with an ox = to prepare by means of good; to plough with a donkey = by means of truth; (and) in a state of good are all those in the Celestial Kingdom; but in a state of truth are all those in the Spiritual Kingdom; and he who is in the one cannot be in the other.
He who learns Truths and does them, is like one who sows his seed and ploughs it down.
Will he plough with oxen? () = is there any perception of good?
To plough to sow () = to learn.
The ploughman reaching the reaper = that he who receives good... shall also perform use; thus that they will be together with the man of the Church.
Elisha ploughing with twelve yoke... = the formation of the Church through truths from good from the Word.
Oxen ploughing () = the will of good.
